subscribers.title: Subscribers
subscribers.content:
Subscribers is iQIYI's disclosed subscribing-member count for the period, in millions.

For iQIYI, Inc.: membership fees are the company's largest and stickiest revenue line; iQIYI stopped disclosing this number after FY2022, so the chart ends there -- a disclosure change, not a business collapse.

What to watch:

  • Growth or decline through FY2022, the last reported data
  • Management commentary on subscriber trends in filings since, now that the number itself is withheld

arpu.title: ARPU (average revenue per user)
arpu.content:
ARPU is average monthly membership revenue per subscriber, in RMB.

For iQIYI, Inc.: ARPU rising while subscriber growth slows is a price/mix lever, not volume; it also stopped being disclosed after FY2022, same as the subscriber count.

What to watch:

  • ARPU trend through FY2022 relative to subscription-revenue growth since (a proxy once ARPU itself goes dark)
  • Price increases versus discounting/bundling that cuts the other way

revenueMix.title: Revenue mix
revenueMix.content:
iQIYI's revenue splits into membership (subscription), online advertising, content distribution (licensing content to third parties) and other (IP licensing, games, e-commerce).

For iQIYI, Inc.: membership has become the clear majority of revenue as advertising has stayed roughly flat -- the mix shift matters because membership revenue is subscription-like and advertising is cyclical and tied to content slate timing.

What to watch:

  • Membership share of total revenue trending up or down
  • Advertising swings around tentpole content releases
  • Distribution revenue, which is lumpy and deal-driven

contentCost.title: Content cost
contentCost.content:
Content cost is amortisation of licensed and self-produced content plus production cost of self-produced content -- the single largest expense line for a streaming platform.

For iQIYI, Inc.: the path to profitability has been holding content spend roughly flat to declining in absolute RMB while revenue grows, i.e. the ratio on the right axis falling -- the clearest single operating-leverage signal in the business.

What to watch:

  • Content cost / revenue falling (operating leverage) versus rising (content arms race)
  • Absolute content spend relative to the content slate driving subscriber and ad-revenue swings

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For iQIYI, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For iQIYI, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For iQIYI, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For iQIYI, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For iQIYI, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For iQIYI, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For iQIYI, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For iQIYI, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For iQIYI, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
